facts.fact: Kasugataisha is a Shinto shrine associated with the Fujiwara family, established in 768, with a wooded lantern approach and vermilion buildings.
facts.excerpt: ze lanterns hung throughout the shrine, are lit up from sunset. Visitors can join morning prayers (omairi) at 9:00 every day. The shrine was built in 768 by the Fujiwara clan, which dominated Japanese politics until the 11th century. There are four main deities enshrined, including Takemikazuchi no Mikoto who, according to legend, traveled from Ibaraki in Northern Japan on a white deer to dwell on Mt Mikasa, above the shrine.
